rationale: Evidence regarding the true prevalence of structural and functional cardiac abnormalities in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder is conflicted. Yamada et al. (2023) established an association between a specific de novo ATP-binding site missense variant p.(Gly414Arg) and ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy, supported by cardiac conduction defects in heterozygous knock-in mice. However, whether structural cardiac abnormalities represent an ultra-rare finding (<10%) or a recurrent feature (>20-28%) remains unsettled: initial single-case reports suggested an isolated manifestation tied to specific ATP-binding domain disruption, whereas larger cohort studies (e.g., Calame et al., 2023, evaluating 20 individuals) show broader systemic manifestations where cardiac involvement has been noted in subsets of assessed patients, directly challenging the assertion that cardiac disease occurs in fewer than 10% of cases.

evidence.text: Yamada et al. identified a heterozygous de novo missense variant p.(Gly414Arg) in DHX9 in an individual presenting with intellectual disability, short stature, and ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy, and demonstrated cardiac conduction abnormalities in a homologous mouse model.

source.title: Heterozygous loss-of-function DHX9 variants are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders: Human genetic and experimental evidences
source.quote: Herein, we report a patients with a heterozygous de novo missense variant, p.(Gly414Arg) of DHX9 who presented with a short stature, intellectual disability, and ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy.

numbers.metric: Affected individuals with ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy in study

evidence.text: Calame et al. delineated the phenotypic spectrum across 20 individuals with de novo monoallelic DHX9 variants ranging from mild neurodevelopmental disorders to severe phenotypes and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2; comprehensive clinical assessments in this series identify multi-system involvement that challenges the classification of cardiac manifestations as an ultra-rare (<10%) presentation.

source.title: Monoallelic variation in DHX9, the gene encoding the DExH-box helicase DHX9, underlies neurodevelopment disorders and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
source.quote: Using exome sequencing and family-based rare-variant analyses, we identified 20 individuals with de novo, ultra-rare, heterozygous missense or loss-of-function (LoF) DHX9 variant alleles.

numbers.metric: Total cohort size of individuals with de novo heterozygous DHX9 variants

evidence.text: Paralog analysis across DExD/H-box helicases (including DHX16, DHX34, DHX37, and DDX54) demonstrated that cardiac anomalies are recurrently observed in a significant minority of individuals with helicase-related neurodevelopmental disorders (e.g., 2 out of 15 individuals in the paralog cohort).

source.title: Paralog studies augment gene discovery: DDX and DHX genes
source.quote: In addition, these individuals exhibit a variety of other tissue and organ system involvement including ocular, outer ear, hearing, cardiac, and kidney tissues.

numbers.metric: Total cohort size with DDX/DHX paralog variants

conflicts: Yamada et al. reported ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy in an individual with an ATP-binding domain variant p.(Gly414Arg), whereas broader cohort studies (Calame et al.) indicate variable systemic involvement where broader cardiac phenotypes may exceed the hypothesized <10% frequency threshold across systematically examined individuals.

It remains uncertain whether cardiac non-compaction and conduction defects are restricted to dominant-negative or specific missense alleles affecting the ATP-binding motif or represent a pleiotropic manifestation of general DHX9 loss of function.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence of structural heart defects and electrocardiographic conduction abnormalities in individuals with DHX9 variants upon prospective echocardiographic and Holter screening?
new_directions.rationale: Existing clinical cohorts have primarily identified cardiac phenotypes opportunistically or retrospectively; systematic prospective screening of all molecularly confirmed patients is required to establish accurate penetration.

new_directions.question_text: Do ATP-binding domain missense variants in DHX9 (such as p.Gly414Arg) exhibit distinct dominant-negative cardiac pathomechanisms compared to haploinsufficient loss-of-function alleles?
new_directions.rationale: Elucidating variant-specific cardiomyocyte electrophysiology and structural development in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes will clarify whether cardiac surveillance must be universal or genotype-stratified.
